work.title: Set up team workflow
work.label: setup
work.description: Get the repo ready for three people working through pull requests. Do this together before splitting up.

children.title: Check the starter project locally
children.description: Install the project, run pytest and check the existing CI run. Record what is failing before changing anything.
children.done_when: Everyone can run the project locally and we know the starting point.

children.title: Add collaborators and protect main
children.description: Invite the other two group members. Require pull requests and at least one review before merging. Check what protection rules the repo plan supports.
children.done_when: Direct pushes to main are restricted and someone else reviews each PR.

children.title: Agree on branches and reviews
children.description: Use small feature branches, link PRs to issues and review each other’s changes. Each person should create and review at least one merged PR.
children.done_when: All three have a clear way to contribute and review changes.

work.title: Run code checks in CI
work.label: ci
work.description: Start with the tests in tests/ and the existing workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Keep changes small.

children.title: Fix the test environment
children.description: Review Python version and dependency installation in the current workflow. Use the project’s dev dependencies for tests.
children.done_when: The test job can run on a clean GitHub runner.

children.title: Run tests on pull requests
children.description: Run the code tests for pull requests and updates to main. Keep failures visible in the PR.
children.done_when: A failing test makes the CI check fail.

children.title: Check a deliberately failing test
children.description: Confirm that a broken assertion produces a red workflow run. Revert the test change afterwards.
children.done_when: There is a recorded passing and failing run.

work.title: Validate training data
work.label: data
work.description: Check data/kundbas.csv before model training. Validation should fail with a useful error, not silently drop bad rows.

children.title: Define data checks
children.description: Check required columns, types, missing values and sensible values for the target. Base the rules on the actual dataset.
children.done_when: Checks reflect the data used by the training code.

children.title: Add tests for valid and invalid data
children.description: Test the expected dataset and at least one broken example, such as a missing column or invalid target.
children.done_when: Good data passes and bad data fails.

children.title: Add a separate data validation job
children.description: Run data validation before training with an explicit dependency in GitHub Actions.
children.done_when: Training is skipped if validation fails.

children.title: Save evidence of a blocked training run
children.description: Trigger a failing validation run safely using test data or a temporary branch. Do not commit broken production data.
children.done_when: The workflow shows validation failing and training not starting.

work.title: Train and evaluate the model in CI
work.label: model
work.description: Use the existing training and evaluation modules as the starting point. The goal is a repeatable model quality check.

children.title: Run model training in the workflow
children.description: Run python -m churn.model after data validation. Check where the model and metrics are written.
children.done_when: CI can train the model from a clean checkout.

children.title: Set a model quality threshold
children.description: Review the existing ROC AUC evaluation and baseline results. Choose or justify the minimum acceptable value.
children.done_when: The threshold has a written reason based on the model and dataset.

children.title: Fail CI when model quality drops
children.description: Run python -m churn.evaluate after training and verify its exit status stops the job on a bad model.
children.done_when: Models below the threshold cannot pass the pipeline.

work.title: Track and save model outputs
work.label: release
work.description: Once training passes, keep the model and the run details together so we can see what produced it.

children.title: Save the model and metrics as an artifact
children.description: Upload outputs/modell.joblib and outputs/matvarden.json after a successful evaluation. Use the paths actually produced by training.
children.done_when: The model and metrics can be downloaded from a successful workflow run.

children.title: Record commit and data version
children.description: Save the Git commit SHA and a checksum or other stable identifier for the training dataset alongside the metrics.
children.done_when: We can link a model artifact to the code and input data it came from.

children.title: Check failed runs do not publish approved artifacts
children.description: Make publishing depend on the evaluation result. Separate diagnostic logs from approved model artifacts.
children.done_when: A failed quality check cannot create an approved model release.

work.title: Build and test the Docker image
work.label: release
work.description: Package the model for a reproducible runtime. Keep the image focused on what the smoke test needs.

children.title: Write a Dockerfile
children.description: Use a compatible Python version and install runtime dependencies. Include the approved model artifact.
children.done_when: The image builds locally and starts without manual setup.

children.title: Add a model smoke test
children.description: Load the model inside the container and run a small prediction or equivalent check using the existing scoring interface.
children.done_when: The container exits successfully only if the model works.

children.title: Build the image in GitHub Actions
children.description: Build after model evaluation and artifact creation, then run the container smoke test.
children.done_when: A bad image fails before publishing.

work.title: Publish a tested image to GHCR
work.label: release
work.description: Publish only from a trusted workflow after all required checks have passed.

children.title: Add registry login and image tags
children.description: Use GITHUB_TOKEN with the right package permissions. Tag the image with its source commit SHA.
children.done_when: The image tag identifies the code version and no token is hardcoded.

children.title: Push only after the smoke test
children.description: Keep the GHCR push behind successful tests, data checks, evaluation and container smoke test. Restrict publishing to main if appropriate.
children.done_when: Failed checks cannot push a release image.

children.title: Pull and check the published image
children.description: Pull the GHCR image by its immutable tag and run the same smoke test.
children.done_when: The registry image works outside the build job.

work.title: Verify the full pipeline and document it
work.label: docs
work.description: Test the complete path and write down how to run it and what each job protects.

children.title: Run the full workflow from a pull request
children.description: Open a PR and follow the checks from code tests to model evaluation. Confirm the final publishing policy works as intended.
children.done_when: There is a green run covering the agreed checks.

children.title: Document local commands and pipeline stages
children.description: Update README with setup, tests, train/evaluate commands, workflow diagram or short stage list, and how to find artifacts and images.
children.done_when: Someone outside the group can understand and run the project.

children.title: Check PR contributions and final submission
children.description: Make sure everyone created and reviewed a merged PR. Collect relevant links, screenshots and any requested individual reporting.
children.done_when: The group can demonstrate the pipeline and each person’s contribution.

work.title: Measure and improve the pipeline
work.label: vg
work.description: Only start after the shared pipeline works. Each person chooses two measurable improvements for their own analysis.

children.title: Person A: measure CI improvements
children.description: For example, investigate dependency caching or job duration. Record baseline and new timings from comparable runs.
children.done_when: Two changes are explained with before/after results.

children.title: Person B: measure reliability or image size
children.description: For example, reduce image size or improve smoke test coverage. Use measurements rather than assumptions.
children.done_when: Two changes are explained with before/after results.

children.title: Person C: measure data or release robustness
children.description: For example, test a changed data schema or safer release tagging. Show what fails before and after.
children.done_when: Two changes are explained with before/after results.
